resources.string: Flash an nRF Bluetooth module, a remote or another chip through the controller\'s SWD header

The controller acts as an SWD probe (firmware with the Black Magic probe built in). Wire the target\'s SWDIO, SWCLK, GND and 3.3 V to the controller\'s SWD header, or pick the board\'s built-in nRF module.
No ready-made images for this chip
Open a .bin (written at the start of flash) or a .hex file (written at its own addresses).
Read back and compare every block

Erases all of the %2$s\'s flash, writes %1$s and restarts it. Whatever it ran before is gone. Images come from VESC Tool\'s repository and are written as they are; pick the one that matches the module\'s crystal and pins.
Erases all of the %1$s\'s flash. It runs nothing until programmed again.
Flash a VESC Express or other ESP32-C3 / S3 on the phone\'s USB port, also when it no longer starts

Plug the ESP32 into the phone with a USB cable. The VESC Express\' own USB port works directly; boards with a USB-to-serial chip work if that chip is a standard USB serial device. If the board doesn\'t answer, hold its BOOT button while plugging it in.
Simulated VESC Express (try it without hardware)
The firmware archive couldn\'t be reached
Pick the three files below instead, or connect to the internet and reconnect.
The archive has no VESC Express builds for this chip
Erases the stored script or screen. Use it when a package or script stops the Express from starting.

Writes the bootloader, partition table and app (%1$s), checks each with the chip\'s MD5, then restarts it. Settings stored on the Express stay. Keep the cable plugged in until it finishes; if it is interrupted, connect again and flash again.
Flashed, checked and restarted. Connect to it from the connect screen.
Turn a font into the bitmap font files LispBM display drivers load
Renders the printable characters into fixed-size glyphs and saves them as a .bin file in the format of VESC Tool\'s display tool, for loading from a LispBM script.
